The USB 2.0 interface shall prevent unauthorized access to data and ensure system stability by detecting and isolating electrical faults (such as shorts or overloads), rejecting invalid file system structures, and blocking execution of malicious code within a maximum response time of 10 milliseconds after fault detection.

The system shall provide continuous electrical power to all assembly equipment throughout the entire assembly duration, ensuring that no fault condition results in an electric current path between any energized component and the vehicle body structure.

The contractor shall define fault setting conditions (e.g., open-load and short-circuit detection) to account for time-dependent system dynamics, ensuring that the logic explicitly incorporates timing thresholds to distinguish transient events from permanent faults.

The control unit shall automatically record a unique fault code in its non-volatile memory upon detection of any short-circuit or open-load condition on any input or output terminal, where the fault code is readable via the system diagnostic interface within 10 milliseconds of event occurrence and remains stored until explicitly cleared by a reset command.

The USB interface shall prevent unauthorized access and data corruption by rejecting malformed commands, isolating electrical faults, and refusing to mount file systems that fail integrity checks prior to any read/write operations.

The system shall prevent unauthorized access to and physical damage of the USB 2.0 interfaces by detecting and rejecting connection attempts that result in electrical shorts, overcurrent conditions exceeding 500 mA, or file system integrity violations, thereby ensuring data confidentiality, integrity, and availability during all operational states.

The device shall withstand a short-circuit condition between any input/output pin, the battery positive terminal, the battery negative terminal (ground), and between any two pins, without damage or malfunction when subjected to a continuous current of 10 A at the nominal battery voltage for a duration of 60 seconds.

The maximum continuous current consumption shall not exceed 300 mA under any of the following conditions: a short-circuit fault between power terminals, or application of reverse polarity to the power input.
The system shall maintain power consumption within the specified limits for all defined operating states, including fault conditions such as incorrect polarity, overvoltage, and short circuits.

The system shall prevent damage to all internal components when exposed to fault conditions defined as input voltage exceeding 120% of nominal rating, input polarity reversal, or output short-circuit current exceeding 5A, for a duration of up to 60 seconds under maximum load.

The system shall limit the output current to a maximum of 50 mA when a short circuit occurs between the output terminal and ground, regardless of the applied input voltage within the specified operating range.

The CPS shall detect and report a fault condition if any of the following occur: an interruption or short circuit in the sensor supply, output, or ground lines; or an internal failure mode within the CPS. This detection must account for the presence of shunt resistances connected to the sensor lines, as defined in Chapter 8.3.2.
The system shall prevent hardware failure or damage resulting from a short circuit between the Control Pulse Line (IN/IFL pin) and either ground or Vbatt.

Electrical interfaces shall be designed such that a single short-circuit fault occurring during component adaptation or handling under voltage does not cause irreversible damage to the system, verified by subjecting the design to specified fault injection tests where no permanent degradation is observed after fault removal.
The system shall detect a primary short circuit or a secondary ECU defect within 5 milliseconds of the onset of a sharp current rise exceeding 10 A/µs.

The system shall detect an open circuit or a short circuit within 10 milliseconds of the fault occurrence, provided the fault resistance is greater than 0 ohms and less than infinity, using a sampling rate of at least 10 kHz.
The system shall withstand an active short-circuit condition for a duration of at least 250 hours without causing damage to any surrounding components.

The electromagnetic device shall limit the fault current to a value less than or equal to 10 A, ensuring that the magnetic flux density remains above the material's coercive force threshold, thereby preventing demagnetization under all specified short-circuit conditions.

The system shall record and store the following parameters for each test cycle: phase resistance, phase inductance, isolation resistance, electrical strength, off-load voltage, short-circuit current, and rotational speed; where the recorded rotational speed must be exactly 500 rpm.

The system shall demonstrate robustness against high-voltage flashover and short-circuit events caused by conductive or insulating particles deposited on surfaces within specified air and creepage distances, as verified by a risk assessment that defines and validates appropriate mitigation measures.

HV components shall maintain air and creepage distances sufficient to prevent electrical arcing and short circuits under maximum specified electric field strengths, even in the presence of conductive particulate contamination; compliance shall be verified by demonstrating that measured breakdown voltages exceed the design voltage multiplied by a safety factor of 1.5 when tested according to IEC 60529 with defined levels of conductive dust.

The Charge Coupler Interface Connector's Control Pilot and Proximity/Pins shall be constructed with insulation and protective mechanisms capable of withstanding a direct short circuit to the AC supply line for a duration of 1 second without resulting in fire, explosion, or permanent damage to the connector assembly.

The High-Voltage Interlock Loop (HVIL) shall be considered in a safe state if and only if the loop is electrically continuous and the monitored voltage at the controller input exceeds 10 V; otherwise, the system shall detect an open-loop condition, a short circuit to Low Voltage positive, or a short circuit to vehicle ground.

The charging cable lock shall not allow current flow between the positive terminal and any other conductor when the device is in the locked state, as verified by applying 12 V DC across the terminals and measuring zero current with a precision of ±0.1 mA.
The OBC shall detect a short circuit between the Charge Coupler Flap signal line and ground within 10 milliseconds of the fault occurrence, provided the fault current exceeds 5 mA.

The socket flap locking mechanism shall not exhibit an electrical continuity between the lock component and ground when subjected to a 50 V DC test voltage, as measured by a digital multimeter with at least 10 MΩ input impedance.
The pilot function electric circuit shall not experience a short circuit to positive voltage under any operating condition or fault scenario defined in the system safety requirements.

The OBC shall detect a Proximity Input voltage undershoot below the defined threshold and identify this condition as a short circuit to ground within 10 milliseconds, triggering an appropriate fault response.

The system shall detect a short circuit to ground in the contact detection sensor located between the female connector and the charging cable within 10 milliseconds of the fault occurrence, and shall signal a fault status to the host controller.

The on-board charger input voltage sensor shall detect and signal a fault condition when the input voltage line is electrically shorted to the positive terminal, provided that the short circuit current exceeds 10 A for a duration of at least 10 ms.

The OBC shall detect a short circuit between the HVAC input current circuit and ground within 50 milliseconds of the fault occurrence, provided the fault current exceeds 10 A, and shall initiate a protective shutdown sequence immediately upon detection.

The on-board charger input current sensor shall detect and signal a fault condition when the measured current path experiences a short circuit to ground, provided the fault current exceeds 10 A for a duration of at least 10 ms.

The charge level indicator labeled "WHITE" on the on-board charger shall exhibit an electrical continuity between its signal terminal and ground when a short-circuit fault condition is present, and shall not exhibit such continuity under normal operating conditions.

The system shall detect and safely handle any short-circuit condition occurring at any device input, any device output, or within the connected load circuit without causing damage to the system or hazardous conditions.

A short circuit condition for the load output shall be simulated by connecting a resistive load of 0 Ω across the output terminals, where this state represents the lower bound of the defined load range.

The system shall detect and respond to creeping short-circuit conditions defined as a sustained fault current between 90% and 99% of the nominal short-circuit detection threshold for a duration of at least 10 milliseconds.

The system shall detect a short-circuit condition and classify it as either permanent or transient; if classified as permanent, the associated component shall be marked as 'not in service' regardless of its current operational state.

The component shall incorporate a permanently integrated overcurrent protection mechanism that automatically isolates the circuit upon detection of a short-circuit condition exceeding 10 A, ensuring zero current flow within 5 ms and maintaining this state for the component's operational lifetime without requiring manual intervention or replacement.

The Charge Coupler Interface Connector (CCIC), Control Pilot, and Proximity detection system shall maintain functional integrity and prevent hazardous energy release during a short-circuit fault to the AC supply line for a duration of at least 10 seconds, provided that an upstream Type A Residual Current Device (RCD) with a rated residual operating current ($I_{\Delta n}$) of 30 mA and a circuit breaker successfully detect the fault condition and open the circuit within their specified maximum tripping times.

For each electrical pin, apply a short-circuit fault condition to ground and to the upper voltage rail (UB) sequentially, maintaining each condition for a duration of exactly 60 seconds, with no more than a 1-second interval between the end of one test and the start of the next.

The Charge Coupler Interface Connector shall undergo a short-circuit test where each contact and pin is electrically connected to the AC supply line, and the system shall demonstrate no malfunction or damage under this condition.

The On-Board Charger (OBC) shall maintain functional safety and prevent hazardous outputs when exposed to a short-circuit fault within the 12 V vehicle electrical system, including faults occurring in the wiring harness or at the OBC input/output terminals, provided such a fault is electrically feasible.

The Interlock Control Logic (IL-logic) shall detect and signal a fault condition if an electrical short circuit occurs between any two interlock lines, provided the short circuit resistance is less than 10 Ω at operating temperature.

Upon detection of a high-voltage short circuit condition within the system, the High-Voltage (HV) component responsible for monitoring that specific fault shall transmit an Interlock Control Area Network (CAN) message containing the "Short Circuit" diagnostic code to the Vehicle Control Unit within 10 milliseconds of fault detection.

The system shall detect a short-circuit fault within 10 milliseconds when such a fault occurs on any interlock line connecting the signal driver circuit to the high-voltage (HV) component or at the associated signal connector, provided the fault results in a current exceeding 5 amperes.

The system shall detect and signal a fault condition within the interlock circuit if a short circuit occurs between any two conductors, ensuring that this detection constitutes an independent supervisory function distinct from the primary interlock logic.

The DC/DC converter shall automatically transition to the "LOCKED" operating mode upon detection of any fault condition, including but not limited to an output short circuit or a failure in the internal voltage measurement circuitry.

The Load Break Controller (LBC) shall detect an overcurrent condition caused by a load request and respond as follows: if the detected current exceeds the maximum rated output current, the LBC shall limit the output current to the maximum rated output current for a duration of [TBD] seconds; upon expiration of this duration, the LBC shall disable the output to enter a self-protected state.

The System Design Controller (SDC) shall maintain functional safety and prevent hazardous states when exposed to a short circuit on any input or output signal line, provided such a fault is physically realizable within the defined system architecture and wiring environment.

The vehicle battery management system shall automatically determine and execute an optimal relocation strategy for individual cells or the entire battery pack within 50 milliseconds following detection of a crash event exceeding 8 g deceleration, ensuring that all electrical connections are secured to prevent short circuits, containment integrity is maintained to prevent substance leakage, and thermal runaway propagation is mitigated.

The vehicle control system shall detect a crash event, battery malfunction, or an internal/electrical short circuit within 10 milliseconds of occurrence and initiate the appropriate safety response without loss of critical functionality.

The battery design shall prevent cell damage and internal short circuits under all defined operating conditions, including maximum charge/discharge rates, extreme ambient temperatures (−40°C to +60°C), and mechanical abuse events as specified in the test matrix, with no occurrence of thermal runaway or hazardous leakage during verification testing.

The cell block and all internal connections shall remain structurally and electrically intact under specified operating conditions such that no short circuit, isolation failure, leakage current exceeding the defined threshold, or any other critical safety event occurs.

The cell block shall incorporate a switch-off circuit that interrupts the electrical path within 5 milliseconds of detecting a short-circuit condition, thereby limiting the fault current flowing through the battery system to less than 10 amperes.

The battery system shall include a fuse rated for [insert specific rating] amperes that interrupts fault currents exceeding [insert threshold] amperes within [insert time duration] seconds under all specified operating conditions.

The system shall automatically disconnect power via a dedicated fuse upon detection of a short circuit within the battery or high-voltage network; the specific fuse rating and installation location are defined by the contractor's design documentation.

If a fuse is employed to disconnect a short-circuit current within a battery module, it shall be installed in series between Cell 17 and Cell 18; verification shall confirm that this configuration electrically isolates the sub-module containing Cells 1 through 17 from the remainder of the battery pack (Cells 18 through N) upon fuse operation.

The system shall demonstrate that short-circuit protection is verified for a maximum of [N] connected cells, where N represents the highest number of cells in any single series string prior to the activation of the shutdown circuit mechanism.

The main contactors shall open within 50 milliseconds of a short-circuit fault occurring on any phase, as verified by applying a defined short-circuit current to the system and confirming full disengagement of all contacts.

If an overcurrent condition or a short circuit occurs in the TV path, the fuse shall interrupt the current flow; upon successful fuse operation, the main contactors shall automatically open within 10 milliseconds to isolate the fault.
The measurement range shall be dynamically adjusted to a value greater than the nominal maximum if a short circuit is detected; otherwise, it shall remain at the nominal maximum.

The system shall provide a configurable driver feedback signal state (ON/OFF) and accept a short-circuit input signal to enable diagnostic functions, where the diagnostic logic is triggered upon detection of either condition.

The battery supplier shall define a design concept demonstrating that the main contactor and fuse combination can safely interrupt fault currents within 10 milliseconds under all specified short-circuit conditions, ensuring no damage to components or hazardous energy release.

The system shall automatically disconnect the battery terminals from the load within 10 milliseconds upon detection of a short-circuit current exceeding 50 amperes, ensuring that the voltage across the load drops below 2 volts.

The system shall detect and measure short-circuit or overcurrent events within a range of 0 to 500 amperes (AC RMS) with an accuracy of ±[insert specified percentage]% when tested under conditions defined in [insert reference standard/test procedure].

The system shall detect and measure short-circuit or overcurrent events within a continuous range of 250 A to 500 A, with measurement accuracy maintained within ±[specified tolerance]% across the entire range.

The Battery Management System (BMS) shall detect and classify an open interlock loop condition into one of the following three distinct states: 1) Signal loop interruption, 2) High Voltage Interlock Loop (HVIL) signal short circuit to Low Voltage positive (LV+), or 3) HVIL signal short circuit to vehicle ground.

The test specimen shall be placed in a thermal environment capable of maintaining an external case temperature between 53°C and 57°C for a duration sufficient to achieve thermal equilibrium, as verified by a calibrated sensor with an uncertainty no greater than ±0.5°C; immediately upon verification that the external case temperature is within the range of 53°C to 57°C, a short circuit shall be applied using an external resistance measured and confirmed to be less than 0.1 Ω at the time of application.

The system shall maintain a short-circuit condition for a duration of at least 60 minutes, commencing only after the external case temperature of the cell or battery has stabilized within the range of 53°C to 57°C (i.e., 55°C ± 2°C).

The battery management system shall detect a short-circuit condition within the high-voltage battery pack when the State of Charge (SOC) is greater than or equal to 99% and initiate an appropriate safety response within 5 milliseconds.

The system shall withstand a short-circuit fault applied simultaneously across five centrally adjacent modules of the battery unit at 100% State of Charge (SOC) without experiencing thermal runaway, fire, or explosion for a duration of 30 seconds.

The system shall allow short-circuit testing of level sensors (including washer fluid and coolant sensors) while the vehicle is in the fueling state, where the fuel filler flap is open and the refueling process is active.

The system shall provide a graphical representation illustrating the short-circuit current behavior of a Li-ion cell or battery, including the time-dependent decay of current from the initial peak to the thermal runaway threshold.

The system shall disconnect the faulted circuit by operating the component contactor for short-circuit currents below [Insert Threshold] amperes and by operating a fuse for short-circuit currents at or above [Insert Threshold] amperes, where the operation time shall not exceed [Insert Time Limit] milliseconds.

The level sensor system shall successfully complete a short-circuit test without functional degradation or safety hazard when operated under full-fill conditions, defined as the sensor detecting 100% of the specified fluid volume within the designated reservoir.

The high-voltage (HV) fuse shall interrupt the fault current within 10 milliseconds when a short circuit occurs between any two HV conductors or between an HV conductor and ground, provided the fault current exceeds 5 kA at the fuse location.

The fuse shall interrupt any fault current exceeding its rated breaking capacity within the specified time-current characteristic curve, ensuring that the resulting transient overvoltage across the terminals does not exceed 1.5 times the system nominal voltage (1.5 × Un) under all defined short-circuit conditions.
The system shall calculate and measure the overvoltage generated during turn-off under conditions where the inductance is 50 µH and the maximum short-circuit current is 3500 A.

The system shall detect, classify, and store distinct fault events—including delivery interruptions, short circuits to ground, and short circuits to power—for each individual input and output channel across all defined operating states (activated and deactivated). For every detected fault event, the system must record a unique timestamp, the specific fault type, the affected channel identifier, and the current operating state; these records shall be retained in non-volatile memory until explicitly cleared or overwritten by a new event.

The electric drive system shall maintain a safe state defined as either a low-side or high-side active short circuit (AKS) when the low-voltage supply rail is between 3 V and 6 V, regardless of whether the main controller is operational within this voltage range.

The Power Electronic Bridge (PEB) shall deliver a continuous short-circuit current of at least 225 amperes through the electric machine when connected to either the lower or upper Active Knee Switch (AKS), as verified by a test lasting 1 second under rated voltage conditions.

The contractor shall develop a technical proposal detailing specific design modifications or operational parameters required to increase the available short-circuit current at the AKS busbar by at least 10% relative to the baseline case, with the analysis validated using an approved electromagnetic transient simulation model and documented in a formal report submitted for review.

The thermal model shall accurately account for reduced switching losses occurring during active short-circuit conditions on both the high-side and low-side switches; consequently, these losses must be incorporated into the total power loss calculation and used to determine the maximum allowable current.

The system shall detect and flag a fault condition within 10 milliseconds if any internal or external sensor input or actuator output signal exhibits a voltage level indicating a short circuit to ground, a short circuit to the power supply rail, or an open-circuit condition exceeding the specified threshold.

The system shall detect and isolate any short-circuit condition occurring on input or output channels within 10 milliseconds of the fault onset, where the fault is induced by either external measurement equipment connections or internal operating voltages exceeding nominal limits by more than 10%.

The system shall detect a short-circuit condition when the filtered backup battery voltage falls below 2.0 V for a duration of at least 10 ms, provided that the input filter bandwidth is less than or equal to 1 kHz.

If a short circuit occurs in the backup battery path, indicated by the signal BackupShortCircuit being TRUE, the test sequence shall be immediately aborted regardless of the current system state, and the following variables shall be assigned specific values: [insert specific variable assignments here].
PN14_BackupRelay_Rq shall be set to 2 (open) when BackupShortCircuit equals 1, indicating a short circuit in the backup battery path.
The system shall detect a short circuit between any output pin and the VCC supply rail within 50 milliseconds of the fault occurrence, provided that the fault current exceeds 1 mA.

The backup relay shall remain in the open state if any of the following conditions are met: the backup battery voltage is below the minimum threshold for full charge, an internal short circuit is detected within the backup battery, or an external short circuit occurs across the backup battery terminals.

In Lithium mode, the system shall not perform backup battery charge control, decoupled relay diagnosis, backup relay diagnosis, short-circuit detection in the backup path, or increment/decrement operations on relay cycle counters.

If no falling edge is detected within the specified timeout period, the system shall log an error indicating either a short circuit to VCC or that the driver has disconnected the device from the vehicle power supply.

If a short circuit occurs and the driver has exited the vehicle (detected by the door open signal or seatbelt status), the system shall initiate an automatic engine start sequence within 5 seconds of detecting the short circuit condition.

The system shall detect a short-circuit or open-load condition on the M:Acoustic Locking output and generate an "ACK" fault code; the mechanism to set and clear this fault code shall be implemented via a dedicated input signal that transitions from inactive to active for a duration of at least 10 milliseconds.

If the measured power consumption of the cable assembly is less than 0.1 W, the system shall flag a "non-connected cable" status; if the measured power consumption exceeds 5.0 W, the system shall flag a "short circuit" status for either the cable or the active antenna element.

When a short circuit occurs between terminal 30 and terminal 31, or when an open circuit (wire break) occurs in one microphone input channel, the system shall maintain full operational functionality of the remaining unaffected microphone input channel without degradation of performance or loss of signal integrity.

Each microphone input shall withstand a short circuit between the input line and terminal 30 for a duration of at least 60 seconds without failure, where "failure" is defined as any deviation from nominal operation or permanent damage to the input circuitry.

Each microphone input shall withstand a permanent short circuit between terminal 31 and ground for a duration of at least 24 hours without exhibiting functional degradation, physical damage, or thermal failure exceeding 85°C.
The system shall detect a short-circuit fault condition when the current exceeds 90 mA and initiate the defined diagnostic response within 10 ms of detection.

The system shall detect and report a short-circuit fault condition when the measured current exceeds 120 milliamperes (mA) within a maximum response time of 10 milliseconds, provided that the measurement circuit is operational.

The wheelspeed sensor signal line shall not exhibit a short circuit condition between the signal pin and the vehicle battery positive terminal (UBatt) under all operating conditions, including vibration, thermal cycling, and mechanical stress as defined in the environmental test specification.

The wheelspeed sensor supply line shall not exhibit a short circuit to ground under normal operating conditions and after exposure to specified environmental stress tests as defined in [Reference Document ID].

The RF switch output shall be configured in the inactive state when performing a short-to-battery detection test, and shall be configured in the active state when performing an open-circuit or short-to-ground detection test.

The digital output driver shall detect and signal a short-to-ground fault within 5 milliseconds of the fault occurrence, provided the hardware architecture includes dedicated detection circuitry for this condition.

The OBC shall detect a short-to-battery fault on the Charge Coupler Flap input signal within 10 milliseconds of the fault occurrence and set the corresponding Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC) while maintaining the system in a safe state.

The interlock circuit of the high-voltage-on-board electrical system shall detect and signal a fault condition within 10 milliseconds if a short circuit to ground occurs, provided the fault current exceeds 5 amperes.

The OBC shall continuously monitor the battery bus voltage and initiate a fault response if the measured voltage remains below 0 V for a duration exceeding 10 ms, where the short-to-ground threshold is defined as 0 V.

The system shall detect and report a diagnostic fault if the temperature sensor input exhibits any of the following conditions: an open circuit, a short circuit to battery voltage, a short circuit to ground, a signal value below the defined lower threshold, or a signal value above the defined upper threshold.

The voltage threshold for the Charger Coupler Temperature Sensor shall be defined as a short-to-ground condition when the measured voltage at the sensor input drops below 0.5 V, and this condition shall trigger a fault state within 10 ms of detection.

The system shall detect and report a diagnostic fault if any of the following conditions are present on the LED output circuit: an open-circuit condition, a short circuit to battery voltage, a short circuit to ground, or a general electrical anomaly exceeding defined thresholds.
If the proximity signal alternates between a short-to-battery condition and a short-to-ground condition, the system shall set the fault status flag to "active."

The Battery Management System (BMS) shall detect an electrical fault between any battery cell terminal and the vehicle chassis ground when the voltage difference exceeds 10 V, and shall set the Short-to-Ground Fault flag within 5 ms of detection.

The system shall generate distinct diagnostic fault codes when a circuit continuity check detects any of the following conditions: (1) a short to ground, (2) a short to power, or (3) an open circuit; each condition must be uniquely identified by its own specific fault code.

For each sensor channel, the system shall detect and flag an error condition if any of the following are true: (1) the electrical circuit exhibits a short to battery voltage, a short to ground, or an open circuit; (2) the analog signal value is within the physical measurement range but falls outside the defined acceptable operating limits; or (3) the signal exhibits plausibility faults, specifically a stuck-at condition, a bias/shift exceeding the maximum allowable deviation from the expected baseline, or any other condition deemed invalid by the configured plausibility algorithm.

The AHR output shall support continuous open-circuit diagnostics and shall detect short-to-battery or short-to-ground conditions within 10 milliseconds of system initialization, reporting a diagnostic fault status via the defined communication interface.

The device shall provide permanent protection for all four USB interface pins (D+, D-, VBus, and GND) against short circuits to ground and against overvoltage conditions up to the maximum rated USB VBus voltage, ensuring that no damage occurs under these fault conditions as verified by applying specified test voltages and currents.

Upon initiation of a route calculation for a distance not exceeding 50 kilometers, the system shall present the complete route guidance output—including all Active Distance Restrictions (ADRs) and the map display at any supported zoom level—within 1 second of the completion of the calculation process.

If an Integrated Protection Element (IPE) failure occurs concurrently with a loss of coolant condition, the system shall limit the maximum allowable operation time to 10 seconds to prevent thermal damage caused by IGBT losses resulting from a three-phase short circuit.

The system shall initiate a three-phase short circuit by activating all Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistors (IGBTs) located on the same electrical side as the detected faulty IGBT within 10 milliseconds of fault detection.

The EDS shall initiate a three-phase short-circuit condition on the inverter within 50 milliseconds of receiving the command signal, as verified by monitoring terminal voltage and current measurements.

If the panic button is pressed and held for a duration $T \geq 1$ second, the system shall activate the panic alarm; if the button is released before $T < 1$ second, the system shall deactivate any active panic alarm.

The Vehicle Control (VC) system shall exchange data with external entities via the defined communication interface using the specified protocol and message format within 50 milliseconds of receiving a valid request, under normal operating conditions.
